site.title: Sabro
site.tagline: A platform for the Syriac language
site.attribution: Lexicon data enriched with SEDRA, © Beth Mardutho: The Syriac Institute.

home.lede: Sabro means hope — and that's the project: a living home for the Syriac language. Learn it by playing — three free daily games, {meltho}, {mno} and {shmo} — and keep every word they teach.

meltho.heading: Meltho
meltho.body: A Wordle in Syriac — six tries to find the day's hidden word. You don't need to know the alphabet: the keyboard shows every letter's sound as you play.

mno.heading: Mno
mno.body: A daily math puzzle in Syriac numerals — in Syriac, the letters are also the numbers. Build the equation that hits today's target, from Beginner to Extreme.

shmo.heading: Shmo
shmo.body: Guess today's historical figure — from biblical prophets to Syriac Church Fathers. Every guess scores category, era, role, region, tradition and gender against the answer.

library.heading: Every word, broken down
library.body: Browse each word the games have shown — its letters, sounds, root, and meaning in English, French, and Dutch — one at a time.

switcher.scriptNote: Letterforms only — vowels, grammar, and pronunciation follow the West Syriac tradition.

form.name: Name

form.eraHint: Signed century: -10 is the 10th c. BC, 7 is the 7th c. AD. There is no century zero.

form.descriptionsHint: Optional. A sentence or two shown when a round is revealed — never during play, since it would give the answer away. Any language may be left blank.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.metaDescription: How the Sabro ecosystem handles your data: what we store, cookies, your rights, and how to contact us.
privacy.intro: Sabro is a personal, non-commercial academic project dedicated to the Syriac language. This policy explains what data the Sabro ecosystem (sabro.be and meltho.sabro.be) stores about you, and why.

who.title: Who is responsible
who.b1: The Sabro ecosystem is run privately by its owner as a personal, non-commercial project. For anything related to your data, use the contact address below.

data.title: What we store
data.b1: When you create an account, our self-hosted sign-in service (Logto) stores your email address, your username, and a hashed form of your password. We never see or store the password itself.
data.b2: Your profile holds what you set on the profile page: a display name, your preferred language, and your preferred Syriac script.
data.b3: When you play a game while signed in, we store one result per game and day: the date, whether you solved it, and in how many attempts. Playing without an account stores nothing on the server.
data.b4: Our servers keep technical logs (including IP addresses and, for signed-in requests, your user ID) for troubleshooting and abuse prevention. They are not used for profiling and are kept only as long as needed.
data.b5: There is no advertising, and your data is never sold or shared for marketing.
data.b6: We count page visits with Umami, an analytics tool we host ourselves on the same server. It sets no cookies, does not track you between sites, and records no personal data — only anonymous, aggregated figures such as which pages are read and which country a visit came from. Nothing is sent to a third party, which is why no cookie banner is needed.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.b1: We use a small set of functional cookies only: your language and Syriac-script preferences (shared across sabro.be and its subdomains so the apps stay consistent) and a session cookie that keeps you signed in. There are no advertising or analytics cookies — our analytics works without them.

third.title: Third-party services
third.b1: The interface fonts are loaded from Google Fonts, so your browser contacts Google's servers when a page loads; Google may see your IP address in that request.
third.b2: Account emails (such as verification codes) are delivered through Resend, which processes the destination email address for that purpose only.

storage.title: Where your data lives
storage.b1: Everything runs on a server in the European Union (Hetzner, Germany), with nightly backups kept on EU storage — 30 daily and 12 monthly copies, after which they are overwritten.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.b1: You can view and edit your profile at any time on the profile page, and delete your account there too — deletion removes your sign-in identity, your profile and your play results.
rights.b2: You can request a copy of the data linked to your account (an export) by writing to the contact address; you can also ask us to correct or delete anything.
rights.b3: If you believe your data is mishandled, you can lodge a complaint with your data-protection authority (in Belgium, the GBA/APD).

contact.title: Contact
contact.b1: For any question or request about your data, write to contact{'@'}sabro.be.
